summary: Ravi took a 5-carton Maggi order and set up a standing weekly order of 20 Aashirvaad atta bags from Monday, after learning the atta had been out of stock for two days. He mentioned the 10-carton scheme, but Verma ji said he can't stock that much and asked for a smaller scheme, which was not answered. Visibility, competitors and dues were not covered.
score_reason: A solid order and a recurring atta commitment came from good stock-out questions, but the scheme pitch was unclear and unresolved, and visibility, competitor intel and collection were skipped.

coaching.tip: Asking what ran out and sent customers away, then asking how much to keep, turned a stock-out complaint into a recurring weekly atta order. Keep using this sequence.

State the scheme clearly and completely (slab, free goods). When the retailer asks for a smaller scheme, offer the nearest smaller slab from the current scheme list, or promise to check, instead of leaving it unanswered.

Before closing, confirm the atta pack size (customer said 'pack', you said 'bags'). Also quickly check shelf display, pending dues and any competitor offers. Then try one upsell, such as Parle-G or Tata Tea, on top of the Maggi order.

debrief: रवि, वर्मा किराना की विज़िट अच्छी रही। मैगी के पाँच कार्टन और हर हफ़्ते बीस बैग आशीर्वाद आटे का ऑर्डर मिला। बहुत बढ़िया कि आपने पूछा कौन सा माल खत्म हुआ, उसी से आटे का पक्का साप्ताहिक ऑर्डर बना। अगली बार स्कीम साफ़ समझाइए, और जब वर्मा जी छोटी स्कीम माँगें तो लिस्ट से सही विकल्प बताइए। डिस्प्ले, बकाया और प्रतियोगी भी देख लीजिए। अगला कदम: पैक साइज़ पक्का करके सोमवार सोलह नवंबर को पहली आटा डिलीवरी पहुँचाइए।
